clue.text: Flies US painter across Ecuador's capital

indicators.note: one piece is laid across the other, so the painter's name straddles the city

parts.note: Grandma Moses was a celebrated American folk painter
Quito is the capital city of Ecuador

explanation.surface: An American artist travels over the Andes to Ecuador's capital by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecuador's capital' looks like a first-letter pick, but it is the whole city; 'across' means the painter's name is split to straddle it. Grandma Moses was a US folk artist.
explanation.definitionFit: As a plural noun, flies are small winged insects, and these biting gnats are a familiar kind.

clue.text: Result published? To follow

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
to come means to follow later, as in 'the best is yet to come'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the result has been published, then promises it will follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a result is the eventual consequence or end product of something.

clue.text: Ring round during leave

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to quit is to leave a job or place
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A boxing ring is circled during a period of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoit is the metal or rope ring thrown at a peg in the game of quoits.

clue.text: Extremely fashionable black suit

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
spades are one of the two black suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone in a stylish black suit is extremely well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black suit' looks like clothing; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: having something in great abundance, to a very great degree, means extremely so.

clue.text: Merry individual in charge of rowing crew?

parts.note: a single individual is one
being over others means being in charge of them
a racing eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A cheerful person is put in charge of a rowing crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry' here means tipsy, and the idiom for having drunk slightly too much is exactly this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for slightly drunk; merry is the same mild tipsiness after a few drinks.

clue.text: Speak about set wisely

indicators.note: the speaking word goes about, around, the setting word

parts.note: to say something is to speak it
a jelly that has set has gelled

explanation.surface: Advice to speak wisely about some fixed matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: acting like a sage, with good judgment, means acting wisely.

clue.text: Boast about work with the oar

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
to row is to work an oar

explanation.surface: Someone brags about their prowess as an oarsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym verb: to brag or exult loudly over a success.

clue.text: Recording involving old sister with drink problem

indicators.note: the recording takes in, involves, the other letters between its own two

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording
a nun is a religious sister
rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A record tells of an elderly nun with a drinking problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle or puzzling question is a problem that is hard to solve.

clue.text: First hole

definitions.meaning: the first in a series, as in an ... match or ... night
a gap or aperture in something

explanation.surface: Two words: the first hole, perhaps on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the initial occasion and a gap or aperture.

clue.text: German fellow, extreme leader of opposition

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means extreme or excessive

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the start of opposition

explanation.surface: A German man is described as a hardline opposition leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A common German male name, so a typical German fellow.

clue.text: Staunch redhead getting sweetmeat

parts.note: to stem a flow is to staunch it
ginger is British slang for a red-haired person

explanation.surface: A loyal red-haired person is given a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' reads as an adjective, loyal, but here is the verb, to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserved ginger in syrup is a traditional confection, a sweetmeat.

clue.text: Shakespearean heroine's father fencing unlikely trio

indicators.note: fencing in means enclosing, so the father word goes around the rest

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: an unlikely arrangement of the word trio means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine's father fences off an improbable trio of suitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests swordplay, apt for Shakespeare, but means enclosing; 'unlikely' signals the scrambling of trio.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the heroine of The Merchant of Venice, who disguises herself as a lawyer.

clue.text: Clive, an eccentric, reaching a Mediterranean port

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eccentric man called Clive arrives at a port on the Med.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish city and harbour on the Mediterranean coast, an example of such a port.

clue.text: I agree to pick up judge

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it
a judge hears a case in court

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to collect a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliamentary cry of approval used to express agreement with a speaker.

clue.text: Good example to follow part way on line

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
a mode is a way or method

explanation.surface: Advice on taking part along a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose behaviour others copy is a person to emulate, a good example.

clue.text: Changed gear in storm

indicators.note: the word gear is changed, its letters put into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver changes gear in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to rant furiously; the verb sense of fury matches.

clue.text: Small article girl got from Atlantic island

parts.note: the is the definite article
Lena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A little girl brings back an item from an Atlantic island.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote British island in the South Atlantic, famous as Napoleon's place of exile.

clue.text: Chum after ring and gem

indicators.note: the friend word comes after the ring letter

parts.note: a ring has the shape of the letter O
a pal is a chum, a friend

explanation.surface: A friend comes after a ring and a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent gemstone, an example of a gem.

clue.text: Followed translation of EPs? Urdu

indicators.note: translating moves words around, so the letters of EPs and Urdu are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone followed a translation of extended-play records into Urdu.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having chased or gone after someone, one has followed them.

clue.text: Horrified, initially, at message in hostile letters

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of Horrified

parts.note: an email is an electronic message

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified at first by a message within some hostile letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive correspondence sent to a person is mail full of hostility, hostile letters.

clue.text: Deadlock caused by one male behind the times

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
passé means old-fashioned, behind the times

explanation.surface: A stalemate caused by one old-fashioned man.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate where no progress is possible, synonymous with a deadlock.

clue.text: Anger after Foreign Office supplies food for horses

indicators.note: the anger word follows the Foreign Office letters

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, the British government department
rage is extreme anger

explanation.surface: Anger after the British Foreign Office supplies horse feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder, the hay or grass given to livestock, is food for horses and cattle.

clue.text: Tedious talk about border plant

indicators.note: the talk goes about, around, the border word

parts.note: to prose is to talk tediously at length
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Boring chat about a garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a flower bed, apt for a plant, but means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-flowering yellow wild flower, an example of a plant.

clue.text: European on tricky space flight

indicators.note: tricky means complicated, so the letters of space are rearranged into SCAPE

explanation.surface: A European astronaut on a difficult space flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests a space mission; it means running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight in the sense of fleeing from danger is a getaway.

clue.text: Hitchcock's role in Psycho, say, amounted to nothing?

parts.note: came to means amounted to, as in 'the bill came to ten pounds'
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Hitchcock's brief appearance in his film Psycho added up to nothing much.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock appeared fleetingly in his own films; a tiny walk-on role is an example of this kind of appearance.

clue.text: Gang, without leader, argue audibly in court

indicators.note: the squad word loses its first letter

parts.note: a squad is a gang or team

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: to wrangle is to argue

explanation.surface: A leaderless gang argues noisily in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leader' drops S from SQUAD to give QUAD; 'audibly' gives RANGLE, which sounds like WRANGLE since the W is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard enclosed by buildings, as at a college, is a court.

clue.text: Wood by motorway provides food for animals

parts.note: M is used for motorway in Britain, as in the M1
ash is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: A wood beside the motorway supplies food for wild animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of boiled grain or bran fed to livestock is food for animals.

clue.text: One pretty woman, almost the object of worship

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a doll is slang for a pretty woman

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman who is nearly worshipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue or image venerated as a god is an object of worship.

clue.text: Additional clothing fielder required

parts.note: extra means additional
cover can mean clothing, something worn over the body

explanation.surface: More clothing is needed for a cricketer in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, this is a fielding position on the off side, between cover and mid-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielding position, so by extension the player stationed there, a fielder.
